Gate B gains a NON-BLOCKING row: the MPI-458 confirmation run (full test:desktop concurrent with npm start). MPI-458 itself closed as NOT A DEFECT in a5320d67 - the desktop suite does not steal the user's single-instance lock, measured three ways on Electron 41.1.1 - so docs/testing.md needs no waiver, the release notes need no line, and there is nothing to fold. The row exists only so the deferred confirmation is visible instead of forgotten; it was deferred because the live smoke run held the machine, and no source was changed so it cannot regress 1.4. Two decisions inherited onto the umbrella: (1) the proposed CUBRIC_E2E lock exemption was deliberately NOT shipped and must be REJECTED if it returns as hardening - it fixes nothing and would let a spec that forgot CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA boot against the real user profile; (2) a parallel app instance needs BOTH its own profile and its own CUBRIC_PORT - a bare second npm start dies in ~2s, exit 0, silently, which is the lock working correctly and not a bug to chase.

Gate B gains a post-smoke verification session that closes MPI-480 acceptance 3 and MPI-481's live check together - same rig, one throwaway 10 GB volume, ~10 minutes. Recorded because BOTH were proposed as things the running smoke test could absorb for free, and neither can: MPI-481's fix lives in routes/, which is read at server fork, so proving it requires RESTARTING the app that is driving the smoke run, and MPI-480's window needs a Pod deliberately caught cold. Spinning a second app instance is not a workaround - MPI-485 proves an instance that touches the remote engine reaps the other's Pod via the name-based orphan sweep, which is exactly what killed run 3 today. So these are strictly AFTER the matrix finishes. The unchanged hazard is written into the row: cancel with a Pod attached calls remoteUninstallDep and deletes volume partials - delete the Pod first.

Gate A gains MPI-483 and its prerequisite MPI-482, on the umbrella's OWN criterion - 1.4 CLAIMS something that is not true. The wake-up-install bullet at UNRELEASED.md:245 reassures the reader that 'genuine failures - a bad file, a full disk - still report exactly as before', making the disk-full path the trustworthy counterexample the bullet rests on. That path is broken: it subtracts du -sb APPARENT bytes, inflated by aria2 preallocation, and told this run '39.4 GB free' when ~91 GB was. So the fix is either the code or the sentence, and shipping both unchanged is not an option. MPI-482 rides in as the prerequisite (a corrected gate fed by guessed sizes is precisely wrong) and is independently user-visible because modelJob.totalBytes is summed from those same strings on both engines - every 1.4 install bar is denominated by a guess. DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED: MPI-485 (orphan sweep) stays out of the gate list - no 1.4 claim touches it and it needs two instances sharing one RunPod key, which is our situation, not a user's; it is already referenced in Gate B as the reason parallel verification is unsafe. MPI-486 (a partial-install bar looks identical to a downloading one) also stays out - it is renderer-only and therefore parallel-safe with the running smoke test, so it can be worked now instead of gated.
